correctness.rationale: The graph has diameter two, and a forbidden triple is exactly a length-two path with nonadjacent endpoints, taking the path segment between the outermost selected vertices if needed. For triples entirely off the apex the two selected edges must be in one part, and triangle-freeness makes degree at least two in that part exactly the obstruction. Thus deletion of the apex is the join A of the D₂ factors. With the apex present, selected rim vertices must be mutually adjacent and therefore consist of at most one rim edge or a singleton; the link B is precisely the disjoint union of the original rim graphs as one-dimensional complexes. Every D₂ has the full 1-skeleton (a singleton is allowed), so the join of at least two factors is simply connected. The inclusion of each one-dimensional connected component of B is nullhomotopic by contracting a spanning tree and then its cycle loops in A; all component homotopies can end at one point of A. The simplicial inclusion is a cofibration and adding the apex cone is its mapping cone. Replacing the attachment by that constant gives A wedge the unreduced suspension of B. After collapsing a spanning tree in each rim component, the suspension has two poles, one connecting edge per component, and one 2-cell per original loop attached along its corresponding edge and back. Contracting one connecting edge and nullhomotoping those 2-cell maps gives exactly m-1 circles and the sum of the cycle ranks in 2-spheres, without changing the integral homotopy claim to merely a homology claim. D₂(C₄) is K₄ as a graph, hence a wedge of three circles. Reduced suspension of the smash product describes each join up to homotopy, giving 3^m spheres of dimension 2m-1. As an exact small boundary check, two singleton parts give the three-vertex path with GP complex the boundary of a triangle, in agreement with a contractible join and a single circle. The code verify_wheel_bouquets.py uses disjoint rims despite its name; it was inspected, not executed. The source's reported finite checks test faces and mod-two Betti numbers; the m=1 case checks the faces but has no predicted Betti vector in the script. The integral classification is justified by the proof, not by those checks.

value.rationale: The transfer gives actual homotopy information for a natural graph operation and retains any higher topology of the joint dissociation factor, rather than mistaking face counts or field Betti ranks for homotopy. It separately identifies the free fundamental group of rank m-1 and the two-sphere contributions from rim cycles; even with no cycles, multiple rims create circles. The square example illustrates exponential multiplicity in a third degree. The proof uses standard topology economically, but the value is the structural description of the cone attachment over arbitrary allowed factors, not the routine calculation of the square deletion join alone.
